newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower, continues weakness.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower, continues weakness.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Thursday, continuing recent weakness due to moderate air conditioning demand and softness in underlying cash market prices in the West.
"There's going to be more weakness, more softness," a West Coast electricity broker said.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $29.50-$29.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's settlement at $29.96, while September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.50-$22.75 versus yesterday's close at $22.97.
Short-term electricity values in the West remained under downward pressure due to relatively mild weather and plenty of cheap hydroelectric supply in the Northwest.
During early cash activity, firm peak power prices for Friday at PV eased to $28.00-$29.00 and those at COB were steady at $20.00-$21.00.
On the downside, analysts assessed chart support for PV at $29.00 and for COB at $21.60.
They said that the September contracts would rebound and consolidate, if they were able to hold above yesterday's lows.

In the next six to 10 days, forecasters called for temperatures to average above normal in the southern portion of the Southwest while those in Colorado and the California coast would run near seasonal norm.
In the Northwest, cooler-than-normal conditions were expected to spread across the region during the same period.
In generation news, a 600 megawatt (MW) unit at the Grand Coulee hydroelectric dam in Washington was tentatively set for restart today after being shut for repairs earlier this week.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Wash., resumed full output after production was scaled down due to an adjustable speed drive problem.
A 670 MW unit at the Centralia coal-fired plant also in Washington state was expected to be placed on line late Wednesday after shutting Monday for repairs.
Moreover, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie system will be cut again by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours today.
